headline: Discussed the Winooski Equitable Housing Needs Assessment and approved previous meeting minutes unanimously.
summary: Michael Moser presented a housing needs study from the University of Vermont Center for Rural Studies. It covered a resource guide, housing and affordability data, and findings from interviews and focus groups. The report will go to City Council for review and will be added to the Housing section of the Comprehensive Plan.
decisions: Approved previous meeting minutes by unanimous vote.

10/29/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Mike O’Brien, Chair; Brian Colombini; John Baker
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning; Jazmine Hurley, Housing 
Initiative Director
Guests Present: Bryn Oakleaf, Michael Moser
Call to Order by: Mike
Meeting Start Time: 6:37
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: John
Second: Brian
Decision: Voting: Unanimous. Motion carried.
Discussion: Winooski Equitable Housing Needs Assessment
Michael Moser gave an overview of the University of Vermont Center for Rural Studies, and the 
Equitable Housing Needs Assessment project. Michael talked about the project components.
Michael reviewed the resource guide component of the project. Mike O’Brien asked about the 
review process for the project at this point and the next steps. Jazmine said that the 
recommendations will be developed, and the report will be packaged for City Council’s review 
and consideration. Jazmine said that she can review the report, including the recommendations, 
with the Planning Commission after the completion of the report. Mike asked if the resource 
guide refers to municipalities that are comparable to Winooski or in Vermont. Michael said that 
the guide refers to large and small municipalities to connect Winooski’s context with potential 
methods to address the City’s housing concerns.
Michael reviewed the housing and affordability indicators incorporated into the study, and noted 
the differences in Winooski, Burlington, and the state as a whole regarding in the percent of 
population paying more than 30 percent of their income on rent. Michael explained his role for 
the U.S. Census Bureau, and the connection between his role and the state health department. 
John asked about the accuracy of the data. Michael acknowledged the challenges for small 
places with data accuracy, said that looking at data over time helps mitigate the variability in the 
data, and highlighted trends. Ravi asked about the accuracy of the American Community Survey 
versus the decennial census. Michael said that errors in data will always exist especially in small 
places, that the technology to get data is getting better progressively, and that looking at five-
year averages of data increases the sample size and reduces the margin of error. Michael noted 
the importance of using different data sets to establish a narrative.
Michael reviewed interviews and focus groups held for the project. Mike O’Brien asked why the 
target audience didn’t include a wider swath of the public. Michael and Jazmine explained that 
the purpose of the project was to connect with parts of the community who do not participate in 
typical government structures due to language barriers, fear of participation and/or time 
limitations to participate in everyday meetings. Michael highlighted the findings from each of the 
focus groups and interview groups.
Brian asked how this information will align with the Comprehensive Plan work. Ravi said that 
he’ll be incorporating the report into the Housing section of the Comprehensive Plan, and will be 
garnering feedback from the Housing Commission on the draft section in the coming months.
Discussion: Winooski Comprehensive Plan – Safe, Healthy, and Connected People 
section
Mike said that this item is to be skipped due to time. Ravi said that if individual commission 
members have any questions about the draft, they can email him directly.

Mike said that this item is to be skipped due to time. Ravi said that if individual 
commission members have any questions about the draft, they can email him 
directly.
Other Business
Adjourn
